tasks.gr8-financial-literacy-entrepreneurship-: Topic: Financial literacy and entrepreneurship basics. Cover the accounting cycle from source documents through journals and ledgers, cash receipts journal, general ledger posting, and the four factors of production in entrepreneurship. Ask Grade 8 learners to trace transactions through the accounting system, record journal entries correctly, classify entrepreneurship factors, and justify business decisions based on financial literacy principles.
tasks.gr8-accounting-cycle-statements-t2: Topic: The accounting cycle of a service business. Cover the steps (transactions, source documents, cash journals, General Ledger, Trial Balance, Income Statement, Balance Sheet), the trial balance with debit total equal to credit total, the Income Statement (income minus expenses gives net profit or loss; equipment is an asset, not an expense) and the Balance Sheet (assets equal owner's equity plus liabilities; owner's equity is capital plus net profit). Use the same small business: capital R10 000, fees R7 000, expenses R3 100, equipment R2 000, bank R11 900, net profit R3 900. Ask Grade 8 learners to compute profit, equity and total assets.
tasks.gr8-cash-receipts-journal-t2: Topic: The Cash Receipts Journal (CRJ) of a service business. Cover its purpose (money received), the columns (date, document number, details, Bank and analysis columns such as Fees earned and Capital), source documents (receipts, deposit slips), entering receipts, closing off by totalling and cross-casting (Bank column equals the analysis columns), and the effect on the accounting equation (bank and owner's equity increase). Ask Grade 8 learners to total the Bank column, choose the analysis column and state the effect on the equation.
tasks.gr8-factors-markets-t2: Topic: Factors of production and markets. Cover capital (own and borrowed), labour (unskilled, semi-skilled, skilled; the role of workers; fair employment practices), natural resources, entrepreneurship and remuneration (rent, wages, interest, profit), the goods and services market and the factor market (labour and financial markets). Ask Grade 8 learners to match factors to rewards, classify markets and compute a simple wage bill.
